title: Exactness of the explicit transported boundary of an injectively exact square
statement: Let C and an injectively exact square S of additive group-valued functors be as in [lem-sc-injectively-exact-square-resolution-short-exact]. Use the explicit transported boundary b_S(F,n) defined there, not an existentially chosen connecting map. For every F, the degree-zero derived diagonal R^0 A(F) -> R^0 B(F) x R^0 C(F) is injective. For every F and n>=0, the resulting sequence with derived diagonal, derived difference, and this b_S(F,n) is exact at the product R^n B(F) x R^n C(F), at R^n D(F), and at R^{n+1} A(F). There is no naturality assertion in this statement; it concerns the homological exactness of the fixed explicit maps.

proof.text: For the explicitly defined resolutionSequence and transported boundary of [lem-sc-injectively-exact-square-resolution-short-exact], Use [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] to form the connecting map H^n(D(I^bullet)) -> H^{n+1}(A(I^bullet)). Transport through the injective-resolution comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift]. Homology of the termwise binary product is the binary product of homologies: both cycles and boundaries split coordinatewise, so the quotient comparison and its inverse are induced by the two projections and the two inclusions. Under this comparison the first map is the pair of the derived a and b, and the second is derived c minus derived d, by additivity of homology. The three homology exactness positions therefore give the three Function.Exact assertions. In degree zero no incoming boundaries exist, so homology is the kernel of the outgoing differential. A termwise injective diagonal restricts to an injective map between these kernels; this gives the initial Function.Injective assertion.

lean.statement:
theorem boundary_exact (S : InjectivelyExactSquare.{u, v, w} C) :
    (∀ (F : C),
        Function.Injective (fun x : (S.X₁.rightDerived 0).obj F ↦
          ((NatTrans.rightDerived S.f₁₂ 0).app F x,
            (NatTrans.rightDerived S.f₁₃ 0).app F x))) ∧
    (∀ (F : C) (n : ℕ),
        Function.Exact
          (fun x : (S.X₁.rightDerived n).obj F ↦
            ((NatTrans.rightDerived S.f₁₂ n).app F x,
              (NatTrans.rightDerived S.f₁₃ n).app F x))
          (fun x : (S.X₂.rightDerived n).obj F × (S.X₃.rightDerived n).obj F ↦
            (NatTrans.rightDerived S.f₂₄ n).app F x.1 -
              (NatTrans.rightDerived S.f₃₄ n).app F x.2) ∧
        Function.Exact
          (fun x : (S.X₂.rightDerived n).obj F × (S.X₃.rightDerived n).obj F ↦
            (NatTrans.rightDerived S.f₂₄ n).app F x.1 -
              (NatTrans.rightDerived S.f₃₄ n).app F x.2)
          (S.boundary F n) ∧
        Function.Exact (S.boundary F n)
          (fun x : (S.X₁.rightDerived (n + 1)).obj F ↦
            ((NatTrans.rightDerived S.f₁₂ (n + 1)).app F x,
              (NatTrans.rightDerived S.f₁₃ (n + 1)).app F x)))
